limitations: A live response proves provider text was processed, not that every word of a full song has a manually reviewed reading.
Independent ISO/song excerpt checks preserve vowel length, retroflex letters, nasalization and Georgian ejective apostrophes; live comparisons allow source case/punctuation differences only.
Unvowelled Arabic checks script transliteration only; unwritten vowels and dialect cannot be recovered from consonants.
Shared Cyrillic and Devanagari require compatible trusted hints or distinguishing text evidence; ambiguous passages stay original.
Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam/Odia use ISO 15919 with written-script limits. Odia a denotes /ɔ/; Sanskrit conjunct and loan readings can differ.
Malayalam bare final virama, old ambiguous digraphs and exceptional singer/dialect voicing are not guessed; atomic chillus and explicitly written half-u are handled.
Mandarin Pinyin does not supply Cantonese readings or all singer-specific poetic pronunciations.
Provider matches use known title/artist aliases and edition gates; externally matched Deezer recordings additionally supply the duration gate.

Tamil uses a conventional hybrid guide: written vowel/consonant distinctions, supported contextual voicing, 62 exact reviewed initial choices and 1,123 strictly filtered Dakshina initial preferences. Other loans, compounds, c/s choices, dialects and singer elisions retain conservative spelling readings; full-song processing does not certify every sung word.
